title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
commits: Initial: add autotune defaults for batching and caching (autotune/manager)
Add quantization profile registry and selection heuristics (autotune/profiles)
Wire unit-econ metrics into Console and backend telemetry
Add CLI tool for running autotune sweeps and exporting recommendations
Fix test flakiness around cache key lifecycle and batch window timing
Address review feedback: telemetry labels, safety guards and canary thresholds
description:
Context: We have multiple customers and internal benchmarks indicating that sensible defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles drive substantial unit-cost savings without user intervention. This PR consolidates previous experimental work (ENG-5421) into a production-ready autotune defaults package and adds unit-econ tooling so operators can measure expected token-cost improvements before rollout.

Motivation: Reduce customer cost by making batching/caching/quantization recommendations automatic and observable. Many teams either run with conservative defaults or manually tune per workload; providing safe defaults + tooling should reduce per-token costs and help sales/CS demonstrate ROI.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds an autotune manager that computes and applies recommended defaults for batching window, batch size heuristics, and KV/prefix cache retention policies.
- Introduces a quantization profile registry with heuristics to pick the smallest profile that passes quality/regression checks for a given model family and sequence-length distribution.
- Adds a small CLI (cli/autotune_cli.py) to run local canaries and emit recommendations as YAML for Console/import.
- Plumbs unit-economic metrics (cost-per-token estimates, expected savings, RU equivalence) to the Console dashboard and backend telemetry.
- Adds safety guards: canary rollout flag, rollout thresholds, and automatic fallback to pinned configs when quality regressions are detected.

Checklist:
- [x] core autotune manager implementation and integration with runtime routing
- [x] quantization profile registry + selection logic
- [x] Console dashboard for unit economics + export/import of recommendations
- [x] CLI tooling for local canaries and sweep scripts
- [x] tests for default heuristics and telemetry reporting
- [x] docs and changelog (docs/autotune.md)

Testing and benchmarking:
- Ran internal perf canary across 3 model families (small/medium/large) with synthetic workloads and a small production canary on dedicated pool. Observed median cost reduction of 18-28% depending on workload mix. See attached benchmark summary (internal link in Linear).
- Unit and integration tests added; initial CI run failed on a timing-sensitive test (test_autotune_defaults) which I fixed by mocking the batch window clock.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind "autotune_defaults" feature flag (off by default for existing customers).
- Deploy to staging, run 1-week canary on selected customers on Dedicated, monitor unit-econ dashboard and quality regressions.
- Enable automatic rollout after stability window and opt-in conversions.

Notes: This PR intentionally does not enable autotune by default for hosted customers; separate work will add a self-serve opt-in flow.
